idiom_name: one EventEmitter/queue/module per message type, with a per-type handler
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no static types, so the binding is one object per message type plus a convention: a dedicated EventEmitter, array or in-process queue for each type, with handlers registered on it, replacing the classic channel object that carries its own type name. Because nothing enforces the convention at runtime, each per-type entry point should validate its payload (a schema check) before handing data on; otherwise a producer bug arrives as a well-formed object of the wrong shape on the channel where the consumer trusted the name. Where the channel is a broker (Kafka topic, AMQP queue, SQS queue), the topic name is the channel identity and each consumer subscribes to exactly one topic per message type - the same discipline with a network in the middle.
pitfalls: EventEmitter invokes listeners synchronously and an exception inside one propagates out of emit(), so a failing consumer can break the producer; { captureRejections: true }, try/catch or an explicit queue isolates the two.
Listeners leak when the same emitter is reused across hot reloads or repeated subscriptions: removeListener/AbortSignal is the cleanup, and one emitter per message type keeps the blast radius small.
Nothing checks the payload: without a per-channel validator the 'type' is a naming convention that rots as soon as one producer publishes the wrong object.
